study type: Randomized controlled trial / Experimental intervention study
outcome: Children's food choices (number of healthy foods)
cohort: The study involved 363 children across two separate studies (157 children in Study 1 and 206 children in Study 2).
finding: Computer-based Food-specific inhibition training (FSIT) led to significantly more healthy food choices in children immediately post-training compared to a control group, and FSIT appeared to prevent the decline in healthy choices seen in controls.
